Privileged Access Management
Protecting idx_abcb1923 privileged accounts is paramount during and after migration:
Implement idx_3de19514 Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management for all administrative
roles.
Use time-bound, approval-required role activations instead of permanent role
assignments.
Require phishing-resistant MFA for all privileged operations.
Create dedicated cloud-only administrative accounts that are separate from
synchronized on-premises accounts.
Monitor privileged role activations through PIM alerts and Entra ID audit logs.
PIM has been discussed in detail in Chapter 8, Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management.
Identity protection
Microsoft idx_6e09b0fc Entra ID Protection idx_161d701e provides automated risk detection and remediation:
User risk detection: Identifies compromised user accounts through leaked credential
detection, threat intelligence, and anomalous behavior analysis.
Sign-in risk detection: Evaluates individual sign-in attempts for anomalies such as
atypical travel, anonymous IP addresses, password spray attacks, and malware-linked
IP addresses.
Automated remediation: Configure Conditional Access policies to automatically
require MFA, password changes, or block access based on detected risk levels.
Identity protection has been discussed in detail in Chapter 9, Microsoft Entra ID Protection.
On-premises decommissioning
Once you verify that identity, device management, authentication, networking, and legacy
workloads idx_f06dca4f no longer depend on domain controllers, you can start decommissioning on-prem
AD. The safest path is a staged shutdown. Below is some guidance on how to approach this.

Confirm no service depends on on-premises domain
controllers
The first idx_2cbf8425 step in beginning to decommission on-premises domain controllers is to ensure that
no service depends on them. Below is a checklist:
Identity dependencies: Ensure that no applications require Kerberos/NTLM, LDAP, or
AD DS lookups.
Authentication flows: Ensure that authentication has moved completely to the cloud
and that there are no AD FS servers, no PTA agents, and no password hash sync
dependencies.
Device join state: All devices must be Entra--oined or Entra-registered. No domain
joined or hybrid joined devices should exist.

Group Policy usage: Ensure that all GPOs have been migrated to the cloud.
File/print services: Migrate on-premises file servers to SharePoint and move printing to
the cloud. There should be no SMB shares requiring AD authentication.
DNS dependencies: No internal DNS zones are tied to domain controllers.
Certificate services: No AD CS templates, auto-enrollment, or domain-joined PKI.
SCCM/ConfigMgr: Ensure no devices are managed using ConfigMgr or co-managed.
RADIUS/NPS: Move Wi-Fi authentication to Entra ID.
Performing these checks prevents surprises later.
Validate Entra ID is the authoritative source
The next idx_603d0afb step is to make Entra ID authoritative for users, groups and devices. The following is a
useful checklist.
User lifecycle: Ensure that users are created and managed directly in the cloud.
Group lifecycle: Ensure that groups are created and managed directly in the cloud.
Access policies: Configure appropriate Conditional Access and identity protection
policies.
App idx_73007a62 authentication: Confirm that all applications use OIDC/SAML and no application
depends on Kerberos.
Device compliance: All devices should be managed using Intune.
Once it is confirmed that Entra ID is the source of authority, you can begin removing on-prem
components.

Chapter 17 594
Remove hybrid identity components
If idx_8aaa5d59 you used hybrid identity, remove these in order:
Microsoft Entra Connect: This involves disabling synchronization to Microsoft Entra
and uninstalling Microsoft Entra Connect from the server it was installed on.
PTA agents: If you had configured Pass-Through Authentication, remove all agents.
AD FS: Migrate all relying parties to Entra and decommission the AD FS farm.
Once the hybrid dependencies are removed, ensure that there are no on-premises services
depending on Active Directory.
Clean up the domain
Once idx_afa3866a dependencies are gone, ensure that there are no more servers that are joined to the Active
Directory domain. Once done, remove all forest and domain trusts and remove entries from
Active Directory sites and services entries.
Decommission domain controllers
The last idx_bdf9bfa3 step is to start decommissioning domain controllers. Depending on the number of
domain controllers this activity could take several days or weeks. The following steps should
be taken in order:
Transfer all FSMO roles to a single DC
Demote secondary DCs
Demote the final DC
Remove AD DS role
Power off
As a final cleanup step after decommissioning domain controllers, ensure that all AD DNS
zones, DNS records, DHCP scopes, and client references to domain controllers are removed.
Summary
Migrating from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID is one of the most
significant infrastructure transformations an organization can undertake. It touches every
user, every device, and every application in the environment. Success requires a methodical
approach that combines thorough planning, the right migration strategy, robust security
practices, and continuous validation. This chapter discussed the states of migration and
migration strategies and provided detailed guidance to migrate from Active Directory to
Microsoft Entra ID. The journey from Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID is not a single
event but an ongoing transformation. Organizations that approach it with discipline, patience,

A career built on Microsoft Entra expertise is becoming one of the most dynamic and future-

Zero Trust architectures, they increasingly rely on professionals who can design, secure, and
govern identity at scale. Entra sits at the center of this shift: it is no longer just an identity
platform, but the control plane for access, trust, and digital safety across hybrid and multi-
cloud environments. This chapter explores how Entra skills open doors to roles that blend
technical depth with strategic influence, from identity engineering and access governance to
AI-driven security operations and cross-cloud compliance.
The demand for Entra-literate talent is rising because identity has become the new perimeter.
Companies need people who can translate business risk into policy, automate lifecycle
management, integrate diverse applications, and build resilient access strategies that support
both human and machine identities. These capabilities are now essential in cybersecurity,
cloud architecture, DevOps, and emerging AI governance roles. Whether you are early in your
career or looking to pivot into a high-impact domain, mastering Entra positions you at the
intersection of security, innovation, and organizational trust.
This chapter maps Microsoft Entra skills to real job roles and career paths, showing where
identity fits in modern security and cloud programs, and how to translate hands-on Entra
experience into job-ready capability. It is intended for:
Early-career IT pros who want a clear set of identity-focused entry points and portfolio
projects.
Experienced IT pros who want to pivot into identity, improve seniority, or broaden
scope into Zero Trust and cloud security programs.

The Entra leverage
The market signals are unambiguous. According to MarketsandMarkets, the global identity
and access management market was valued at approximately $25 billion in 2025 and is
projected to reach $42 billion by 2030, growing at a compound annual rate of 10.4 percent.

recognized leader in IAM and the Entra platform's deep integration with Microsoft 365 and
Azure means that professionals who master these tools find themselves at the intersection of
the two largest enterprise software ecosystems in the world. For professionals considering

Entra architecture, governance, lifecycle automation, and privileged access patterns.
Experience driving platform strategy, managing service health, aligning stakeholders, and
guiding engineering teams is essential to operate confidently at this level.
Key skills and certifications by career level
Each idx_5e4c8d71 stage of the IAM career demands a distinct combination of technical skills, certifications,
and professional competencies. Understanding these requirements allows professionals to
invest their development time strategically.
At the early-career level, the foundational certification is the SC-900: Microsoft Security,
Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals. This entry-level credential validates

Soft skills at this stage center on communication, documentation, and systematic

Mid-career professionals should pursue the SC-300: Microsoft Identity and Access
Administrator Associate, which validates the ability to design, implement, and operate

Technical skills at this level expand to include infrastructure-as-code, API integration, identity

Senior professionals benefit from the CISSP and CCSP for broad security leadership credibility,
combined with deep platform expertise validated by other advanced certifications. The
Certified Identity and Access Manager credential from the Identity Management Institute
validates expertise in identity governance and access control at the strategic level. At this tier,
the most idx_18ca7241 critical skills are architectural thinking, vendor evaluation, regulatory compliance
expertise, executive communication, and the ability to translate complex identity concepts into
business value.

Career progression paths in identity management
The identity idx_1f87b9ea and access management career does not follow a single linear path. Instead, it
branches into several distinct trajectories, each offering compelling opportunities for growth
and specialization.
Technical architecture track
The idx_dc2cf136 Technical Architecture idx_ebe7b225 track progresses from Junior IAM Engineer to IAM Engineer to
Senior IAM Engineer and ultimately to Principal Identity Architect. This path rewards deep
technical expertise and the ability to design identity solutions that scale across complex,
multi-cloud environments.

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 18 610
chunks.content:
Chapter 18 610
Operations and platform leadership track
The idx_7d934d22 Operations and Platform Leadership track idx_00cad871 moves from Identity Support Analyst to Entra
Administrator to IAM Operations Manager and into Director of Identity Services. Professionals
on this path excel at running identity platforms reliably, managing teams, and ensuring
compliance. This track emphasizes operational excellence, incident management, and the
ability to maintain identity services at enterprise scale.
Security and strategy track
The idx_038f0024 Security and Strategy idx_42d200e5 track evolves from Cloud Security Associate to Cloud Security
Engineer to IAM Strategy Lead and into CISO or VP of Security. This path suits professionals
who view identity as one dimension of a broader security mission and who aspire to shape
organizational security strategy at the executive level.
Consulting and advisory track
The Consulting and Advisory track offers a parallel path through firms like Avanade, Deloitte,
and idx_906190e6 Accenture, where idx_36035162 professionals advise multiple organizations on identity transformation.
Consulting roles often offer accelerated exposure to diverse environments and technologies.
The future of identity-focused careers
The identity profession is not merely growing; it is transforming in ways that will create
entirely new categories of work over the coming decade. Three forces are reshaping the
landscape, and professionals who position themselves at the intersection of these trends will
find themselves in extraordinary demand.
The explosion of non-human identities
The first force is the explosion of non-human identities. AI agents, service principals, workload
identities, IoT devices, and automated workflows now outnumber human identities. Microsoft
has described this as the expanding identity perimeter, noting that non-human identities are
often highly privileged, reducing the need for attackers to escalate their own access.
A specialist who understands how to secure AI agents using Workload Identity Federation,
automate the rotation of secrets and certificates, and govern the lifecycle of machine identities
is solving problems that keep CISOs awake at night. Recent industry focus on machine identity
management signals that this is becoming a mainstream enterprise requirement.
Identity meets AI governance
The second force is the convergence of identity with AI governance. As organizations deploy AI
agents idx_cc1c0b5b that fetch data, make decisions, and interact idx_27d4652f with systems autonomously, every one of
those actions requires an identity and an access decision. The professionals who can design
identity architectures for agentic AI workflows, implement consent frameworks for AI-to-AI
611 Career Opportunities with Microsoft Entra Skills

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 18 610
chunks.content:
interactions, and ensure that machine learning models operate within defined permission
boundaries will define the next generation of identity leadership.
Decentralized identity and verifiable credentials
The third force is the maturation of decentralized identity and verifiable credentials. Microsoft
Entra idx_ac5a5909 Verified ID represents an early implementation of this paradigm, enabling organizations
to issue and verify digital credentials based on open standards. As these technologies idx_1e3beb80 mature,
new roles will emerge around credential ecosystem design, trust framework governance, and
privacy-preserving identity verification.
According to Precedence Research, the IAM market's projected growth from $22.99 billion in
2025 to approximately $65.70 billion by 2034 is not merely an expansion of existing roles. It
represents the creation of new professional categories that do not yet have standardized titles.
The professionals who enter and advance in identity management today are not simply joining
a growing field; they are helping to define it.
Your place in the identity revolution
Whether you are a recent graduate exploring your first role in technology, a mid-career
professional idx_43474688 seeking a specialty with enduring demand, or a seasoned leader looking to shape
the strategic direction of your organization, the identity and access management field offers a
path that is both intellectually challenging and professionally rewarding.
The skills you develop in Microsoft Entra and the broader IAM ecosystem are not narrow technical
competencies that risk becoming obsolete. They are foundational capabilities that grow more valuable
as organizations become more digital, more distributed, and more reliant on automated and AI-driven
systems. Every application needs authentication. Every user needs authorization. Every AI agent needs
governance. And every organization needs professionals who can make these systems work securely,
seamlessly, and at scale.
The identity perimeter is expanding, and the professionals who understand how to secure it
are building careers idx_9f76253c that will matter for decades to come. The question is not whether the
opportunity exists. The question is whether you are ready to step into it.
Summary
This chapter explored how emerging trends in identity, security, and cloud technology are
driving increased demand for Entra skills. Key forces such as Zero Trust adoption, AI-driven
governance, workload identity management, and regulatory pressures are highlighted,
demonstrating how they create new career pathways for both newcomers and seasoned
professionals. The chapter outlined the growing importance of areas like lifecycle automation,
privileged access management, and operational excellence. It concluded by recommending

practitioners should leverage their expertise to lead impactful, measurable programs that
